Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

both … and conjunction

also as well as, and also

classical

Liv. 2.12.9: et facere et patī fortia Rōmānum est
Plin. Ep. 9.12.2: cōgitā et illum puerum esse et tē fuisse

et … et

conjunctions, before each member

Each member equal. With a negative, “neither … nor” is nec … nec.

Other words

  • cum … tum — both … and (above all)

    conjunction and adverb: the second member weighs more · also used · classical · Liv. 26.50.13: vincentem omnia cum armīs, tum benignitāte ac beneficiīs

    “Not only … but especially”; often strengthened, cum … tum vērō (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • et facere et patī fortia Rōmānum est

    both to do and to bear brave things is the Roman wayLiv. 2.12.9

  • cōgitā et illum puerum esse et tē fuisse

    remember both that he is a boy and that you were onePlin. Ep. 9.12.2

  • utrumque enim vitium est, et omnibus crēdere et nūllī

    for both are faults, trusting everyone and trusting no oneSen. Ep. 3.4

  • Tum pol ego et oleum et operam perdidī.

    Then, by Pollux, I’ve wasted both my oil and my effort.Plaut. Poen. 332b

  • vēnisse dīs simillimum juvenem, vincentem omnia cum armīs, tum benignitāte ac beneficiīs

    that a young man most like the gods had come, conquering everything by arms and, above all, by kindness and good deedsLiv. 26.50.13

See also and, not only … but also, either … or, neither … nor.
